issues.legal_issue: A civil court cannot hear an injunction suit concerning a waqf or waqf property when the dispute falls within the jurisdiction of the Waqf Tribunal.
material_facts: The plaintiff sued for mandatory and permanent injunctions concerning land admitted by the defendant to be waqf property.
The defendant sought rejection of the plaint on the ground that the dispute belonged before the Waqf Tribunal.
The defendant admitted the waqf and its mutawalli but denied that the plaintiff was a beneficiary, raising a dispute about the plaintiff’s relationship to the waqf.
issues.conclusion: The Waqf Tribunal had jurisdiction over the dispute, and the civil court could not entertain the injunction suit. The appeal was allowed, and the plaint was to be returned for presentation to the Tribunal.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 83(1) and 85 of the Waqf Act, 1995 give the Tribunal jurisdiction over any dispute, question or other matter relating to a waqf or waqf property and bar civil-court proceedings within that field; the jurisdiction does not depend on whether the property’s status as waqf property is disputed or admitted. Section 83(5) gives the Tribunal the powers of a civil court under the CPC. The court relied on W.B. Waqf Board v. Anis Fatma Begum and Akkode Jumayath Palli Paripalana Committee, which support Tribunal jurisdiction over injunction disputes, and on Syed Mohideen for the Tribunal’s power to issue temporary injunctions. It explained that the basis of Ramesh Gobindram v. Sugra Humayun Mirza Waqf was removed by the 2013 amendment and that its narrower approach could not control; it also considered the treatment of the issue in Punjab Waqf Board v. Sham Singh Harike and Kiran Devi v. Bihar State Sunni Waqf Board. The statutory scheme recognizes limited civil-court proceedings in provisions including Sections 68(6), 86 and 90, but none applied to this injunction suit.

predicates.civil_court_injunction_suit: A claimant brought an injunction suit in a civil court.
predicates.dispute_concerns_waqf_or_waqf_property: The parties’ dispute concerns a waqf or property associated with a waqf.

issues.definition: When a civil-court injunction suit concerns a waqf or waqf property, the rule assigns jurisdiction to the Waqf Tribunal.
